newsitem.title: UK: Cuba physical sugar prices firm as crop nears end.
newsitem.headline: Cuba physical sugar prices firm as crop nears end.

text.p: Cuba's sugar shipments programme is still running smoothly but cash prices are gradually rising as regional supplies dwindle before Brazil's return as an exporter, brokers said on Friday.
Taken as a whole, Cuban ports still had good availability from warehouse stocks but interested parties now had to draw on supplies from different ports to make up their cargoes, they said.
Sugar quality is also reported to be good.

"It's still going smoothly but supplies are tightening up so we expect the market to firm from here," said one London trader of Cuban raws, adding that demurrage payments had not been an issue this year.
"The availability of those sugars is going to tail off but there is still some coming to the ports -- it's just that you have to go round all the ports to pick it up now," he said.
Traders quoted Cuban raws at discounts of 35 points bid/25 points offer to nearby futures for May shipment after bid/offer discounts of 53/40 points a month ago.
Cuban physical prices tended to be lower at the start of the export cycle as Havana was anxious to ship quickly to accumulate hard currency and pay for imports of essential commodities such as oil.
But then prices picked up as the crop approached its end and before Brazil's centre-south re-emerges with its 1997/98 campaign, they said.

"It's quite normal that the price starts off in January fairly low and gets gradually higher, especially if it still has some kind of value ahead of anything coming out of Brazil in July," one broker said.
"But people have not been getting as much as they thought they were going to get, so I have to assume they're running out," he added.

Demand has also been slack, and although a steady trickle of Cuban freight orders has been seen into countries such as Iran, there are reports of distressed cargoes in the Black Sea and more Cubans headed that way.
"In the light of limited offtake in the Russian market, demand for this (Cuban) sugar is likely to remain weak," Czarnikow Sugar said in its latest monthly report.

"It's the sort of market where there hasn't really been pressure on them. There hasn't been much demand and all the other origins have been soft-pedalling on their shipment dates," said Chris Pack, analyst at Czarnikow.
Cuba's regional competitors, such as Mexico and Guatemala, have been shifting large amounts of both white and raw sugar this year.
While the whites have been competing with European Union supplies, the raws shipments have depleted the amount of raws available from the region as a whole while Brazil remains absent.
The question is now how much central American sugar is left before Brazil's centre-south starts to ship.
Some central American raws have already been used instead of Cubans, which can present political problems for some traders.
